front: Explain why a contract contains a lease when the customer controls the use of:
back: an identified asset. A lease requires control of an identified asset.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: State the rule resolving a lease is most likely finance when:
back: ownership transfers to the lessee. Ownership transfer is a finance-lease indicator.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Interpret this review point: payment PV of 186 and asset fair value of 190 most strongly indicates:
back: a finance lease because substantially all value is financed. The 97.9% proportion supports finance classification.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Explain why at commencement, a lessee normally records the lease liability at:
back: the present value of fixed lease payments. Initial liability measurement uses present value.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: State the rule resolving five year-end payments of 100,000 discounted at 10% have a PV closest to:
back: 379,079. The ordinary-annuity present value is approximately 379,079.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Interpret this review point: beginning liability is 379,079 and rate is 10%. Interest is closest to:
back: 37,908. Interest equals beginning liability times rate.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Explain why payment is 100,000 and interest is 37,908. Principal equals:
back: 62,092. Principal is payment minus interest.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: State the rule resolving opening liability is 379,079 and principal is 62,092. Closing liability is:
back: 316,987. Subtract principal from the opening liability.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Interpret this review point: under IFRS, most lessee lease expense is presented as:
back: separate interest and ROU amortization. IFRS uses a finance-style lessee model.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Explain why under US GAAP, an operating lease generally presents:
back: a single straight-line lease expense. The operating model produces single lease expense.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: State the rule resolving for a US operating lease, ROU amortization equals:
back: lease expense minus interest. This keeps total expense level.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Interpret this review point: under a finance-style lessee model, principal cash payment is normally:
back: a financing outflow. Principal repays a financing liability.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Explain why for a US operating lease, the entire payment is generally:
back: an operating cash outflow. US operating-lease cash payment is CFO.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: State the rule resolving a finance lessor initially recognizes:
back: a lease receivable and derecognizes the underlying asset. Finance lessor accounting resembles a sale/financing.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Interpret this review point: an operating lessor generally:
back: retains and depreciates the underlying asset. Operating lessor accounting resembles rental.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of leases from the perspectives of lessors and lessees

front: Explain why a defined contribution plan primarily places investment risk on the:
back: employee. The ultimate benefit depends on contribution investment performance.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: State the rule resolving a defined benefit plan primarily places actuarial and investment risk on the:
back: employer. The employer promises the benefit.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Interpret this review point: plan assets are 900 and obligation is 1,000. The balance sheet reports:
back: a net pension liability of 100. Assets minus obligation equals −100.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Explain why plan assets are 1,200 and obligation is 1,050. Funded status is:
back: a 150 net pension asset. Positive funded status is an asset.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: State the rule resolving a lower defined-benefit discount rate generally:
back: increases the obligation. Lower discounting increases present value.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Interpret this review point: employer contributions to a defined benefit plan most directly:
back: increase plan assets and improve funded status. Contributions add plan assets but differ from accounting cost.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Explain why under IFRS, defined-benefit service cost and net interest are generally in:
back: profit or loss. These periodic components affect profit or loss.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: State the rule resolving under IFRS, pension remeasurements are generally recognized in:
back: other comprehensive income. Remeasurements go to OCI.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Interpret this review point: equity-settled stock awards are generally measured using:
back: grant-date fair value. Grant-date fair value anchors compensation expense.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Explain why grant-date fair value is 600 over three years. Annual straight-line expense is:
back: 200. 600 divided by three is 200.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: State the rule resolving option intrinsic value per share when market is 44 and exercise price is 30 is:
back: 14. Intrinsic value is market less exercise price.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Interpret this review point: if market price is below exercise price, option intrinsic value is:
back: zero. The holder will not exercise for a negative payoff.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Explain why higher expected share-price volatility generally makes an employee option:
back: more valuable. Greater upside dispersion raises option value.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: State the rule resolving equity-settled compensation expense is:
back: a real economic cost despite being non-cash. It reduces profit and can dilute owners.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Interpret this review point: a cash-settled share appreciation right is generally:
back: remeasured as a liability. Cash settlement creates a remeasured obligation.
officialLearningOutcome: explain the financial reporting of defined contribution, defined benefit, and stock-based compensation plans

front: Explain why long-term debt due within twelve months is normally presented as:
back: a current liability. The current portion is separately classified.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: State the rule resolving lease maturity disclosures primarily help assess:
back: timing and concentration of contractual payments. Maturities reveal liquidity demands.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Interpret this review point: a pension note should disclose major actuarial assumptions such as:
back: discount rate and salary growth. Assumptions drive obligation measurement.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Explain why unrecognized stock-compensation cost and remaining vesting period indicate:
back: future expense still to be recognized. They help forecast compensation expense.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: State the rule resolving recognizing a lease liability will generally cause leverage to:
back: increase. Debt-like obligations increase.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Interpret this review point: finance-style lease presentation generally makes EBITDA relative to operating presentation:
back: higher. Interest and amortization are excluded from EBITDA.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Explain why lease recognition generally causes asset turnover to:
back: decrease because assets increase. A larger asset denominator lowers turnover.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: State the rule resolving a debt covenant disclosure is important because violation can:
back: accelerate or reclassify obligations. Covenants affect liquidity and classification.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Interpret this review point: stock-option valuation disclosures should include assumptions about:
back: volatility, expected life, dividends, and risk-free rate. These are key option-pricing inputs.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Explain why a pension plan asset allocation disclosure helps evaluate:
back: investment risk and funded-status volatility. Asset mix affects plan risk.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: State the rule resolving a lessee advantage most plausibly includes:
back: flexibility and reduced obsolescence exposure. Leasing can provide flexibility without ownership.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Interpret this review point: non-current long-term debt is usually presented as:
back: a consolidated non-current line with detail in notes. The notes provide instrument-level detail.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Explain why comparing CFO across lessees requires checking:
back: lease classification and framework cash-flow presentation. Classification can move lease cash between CFO and CFF.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: State the rule resolving a large pension deficit should be evaluated together with:
back: assumptions, asset allocation, contribution plans, and maturities. The deficit is sensitive to assumptions and funding strategy.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation

front: Interpret this review point: share-based compensation can dilute owners even when:
back: the expense is non-cash. Equity issuance transfers value to employees.
officialLearningOutcome: describe the financial statement presentation of and disclosures relating to long-term liabilities and share-based compensation
